turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been feeling fatigue and general malaise for the past few months, and I’ve lost about 18 kilograms unintentionally over the last six months. I haven’t changed my diet or exercise, and it doesn’t seem to be improving.
How old are you?
I’m 71 years old. I’ve had the fatigue and malaise for a few months, and the unintentional weight loss has been about 18 kilograms over six months.
Have you noticed any drenching night sweats that require you to change your clothes or bedding?
“No, I haven’t noticed drenching night sweats or needing to change my clothes or bedding.”
Have you noticed a change in your appetite—has it increased, decreased, or stayed the same?
“My appetite feels decreased overall, and I’ve been eating less without intending to.”
Do you have any persistent pain or discomfort anywhere in your body, such as in your abdomen, chest, or bones?
“Not really—no persistent pain in my abdomen, chest, or bones. It’s mainly the ongoing fatigue, feeling generally unwell, and the weight loss.”
Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation, diarrhea, or blood in your stool?
“No, I haven’t noticed any significant changes in my bowel habits—no constipation or diarrhea, and I haven’t seen any blood in my stool.”
Have you had any persistent cough, coughing up blood, or shortness of breath?
“No, I haven’t had any persistent cough, coughing up blood, or shortness of breath.”
Have you had any fevers, or have you been checking your temperature and noticed it running higher than usual?
“No, I haven’t had any fevers that I’m aware of, and I haven’t noticed my temperature running higher than usual.”
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or feelings of hopelessness?
“I haven’t really felt hopeless or had major changes in mood, and I still enjoy my usual activities, but I do feel generally run-down.”
Have you noticed feeling full very quickly after starting to eat, or do you feel full after eating only a small amount of food?
“Yes, I do feel full more quickly than before, and I get full after eating only a small amount of food.”
Have you had any nausea or vomiting, particularly soon after eating?
“Not much—no persistent nausea or vomiting, and I haven’t noticed it happening soon after eating.”
Are you male or female?
“I’m male.”
Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, darkening of your urine, or light-colored stools?
“No, I haven’t noticed any yellowing of my skin or eyes. My urine hasn’t seemed darker than usual, and I haven’t noticed any light-colored stools.”
Have you noticed any swelling or bloating of your abdomen, or does your belly look or feel larger than usual?
“No, I haven’t noticed any swelling or bloating of my abdomen, and my belly doesn’t look or feel larger than usual.”
Have you had any difficulty swallowing, or sensation that food is getting stuck in your throat or chest when you eat?
“No, I haven’t had any difficulty swallowing, and I don’t feel like food gets stuck in my throat or chest when I eat. It’s mainly that I feel full quickly and I’m eating less overall.”
